2027-06-26.title: Sixth Saturday of the Apostles
2027-06-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I promised you in marriage to one husband, Christ
2027-06-26.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The calendar's own headings: “You are betrothed to Christ”; “Do not judge by appearances”. Saturday is kept in many homes as Mary's day.
2027-06-26.verse: Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.
theo: Paul writes to the Corinthians like a father who has arranged his daughter's marriage and now fears for her. “I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” In the customs of the time, the friend of the bridegroom arranged the betrothal and watched over the bride until the wedding day. Paul sees himself in that role: by his preaching he betrothed the Church of Corinth to Christ, and he longs to present her pure on the day of the Lord's coming. His jealousy is “divine”, the jealousy of God himself, who in the prophets calls Israel his bride: “I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy” (Hosea 2:19). The Church is not a club of the like-minded; she is a bride, loved and promised to one Husband. Our Syro-Malabar liturgy speaks often of the Church as the bride of Christ, and the crowning of bride and groom at a wedding is a living picture of that mystery.

Then comes the fear: “But I am afraid that as the serpent deceived Eve by its cunning, your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ.” The danger is not that the Corinthians will abandon religion; it is that they will accept “another Jesus”, “a different spirit”, “a different gospel”, and hardly notice. Certain preachers, whom Paul calls with irony “these super-apostles”, had arrived with fine speech and impressive letters. They offered a Jesus without the Cross, a spirit without humility, a gospel of success. Paul admits, “I may be untrained in speech, but not in knowledge.” The question is never how eloquent the preacher is, but whether the Jesus he preaches is the Jesus of the apostles. In this last week of the Season of the Apostles the warning is timely. Our phones bring us a new preacher every hour; some promise wealth and healing as a reward for money, some mock the Church and the sacraments, some offer a Jesus who never asks for repentance. The bride keeps her devotion sincere and pure by staying with the faith of the apostles, handed down in the Church.

The Gospel takes us to Jerusalem at the Festival of Booths. Jesus goes up to the Temple and teaches, and those who hear him are astonished: “How does this man have such learning, when he has never been taught?” He had not studied under a famous rabbi. In John's Gospel the phrase “the Jews” often refers to the religious authorities of Jerusalem who opposed Jesus; it never condemns the Jewish people as a whole, to whom Jesus, his Mother and all the apostles belonged. Jesus answers: “My teaching is not mine but his who sent me.” Here is the test of every true teacher. “Those who speak on their own seek their own glory; but the one who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true.” Jesus himself, the eternal Word, does not present his teaching as his own invention; it is the Father's. How much more must every preacher, priest and catechist in the Church hand on what was received, and not his own opinions.

Then Jesus speaks of the healing he had done on a sabbath (John 5), which had caused such anger. He reasons with them from their own practice: if a boy may be circumcised on the sabbath so that the law of Moses is kept, why be angry that he made a man's whole body well on the sabbath? And he ends with the line that is today's word: “Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.” The crowd judged by appearances: the man had no degree, so he could not be a teacher; the healing happened on the wrong day, so it could not be from God. We do the same when we judge people by colour, caste, accent, dress, bank balance or the size of their house, or when we decide about a marriage proposal by a photograph. The Lord said to Samuel, “they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart” (1 Samuel 16:7). On this Saturday we look to Mary, the Virgin who was wholly devoted to Christ, whose humble appearance in Nazareth hid the purest heart of any creature. She teaches the Church to be the chaste bride Paul longed for, and to see others as God sees them.
outline: A betrothal, a bride, and the friend of the bridegroom who guards her.
The Church as the bride of Christ; Paul's divine jealousy.
Fine speech and a false Christ; staying with the faith of the apostles.
Teaching that is not one's own; seeing as God sees.
“Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.”
live: Before you share or follow any religious video this week, ask: is this the Jesus of the apostles, the Jesus of the Church and the Gospel?
Notice one person this week whom you have judged by appearance, caste, colour or wealth, and do one kind thing for them.
fathers: The bride of Christ cannot be made an adulteress; she is undefiled and chaste. She knows one home and guards with chaste modesty the holiness of one bedchamber. She keeps us for God.

My teaching is not mine: what is so much yours as yourself, and what is so little yours as yourself? The teaching of the Son is the Word of the Father; so it is his, and yet not his, because he himself is the Word of the One who sent him.
magis: The unity of Christ and the Church, head and members of one Body, also implies the distinction of the two within a personal relationship: the Church is the Bride of Christ, whom he loved and for whom he handed himself over.
The Magisterium is not superior to the Word of God, but is its servant: it teaches only what has been handed on, listening to it devoutly, guarding it scrupulously and explaining it faithfully.
To avoid rash judgment, everyone should be careful to interpret insofar as possible his neighbour's thoughts, words and deeds in a favourable way.
At once virgin and mother, Mary is the symbol and the most perfect realisation of the Church.
saints: Sixth Saturday of the Apostles; in many homes Saturday is Mary's day. Tomorrow: the Seventh Sunday of the Apostles, the last Sunday of the season.

25–30 June: sixth and seventh weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Sun 27: Seventh Sunday of the Apostles, the last Sunday of the season. Mon 28: St Irenaeus, bishop and martyr (also a memorial in the Latin calendar). Tue 29: St Peter and St Paul, the Apostles, an important feast and a day of obligation. Wed 30: in the Latin calendar, the First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church. Looking ahead: the Dukhrana of St Thomas, our Father in faith, on Saturday 3 July, and the Season of Kaitha (Qaita) from Sunday 4 July.
2027-06-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Bridegroom of the Church, you loved her and gave yourself up for her. Keep us, your bride, in a sincere and pure devotion to you. Guard us from every other Jesus, every other spirit and every other gospel, and keep us faithful to the teaching of your apostles. You did not seek your own glory but the glory of the Father who sent you: make us seek his glory, not ours. Give us eyes that do not judge by appearances but see the heart as you see it. Through the prayers of the Blessed Virgin Mary, wholly devoted to you, make us holy and blameless for the day of your coming. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Bridegroom gives himself to his bride. The Church receives the Body of her Lord, and her love is made sincere and pure again. Under the humble appearance of bread and wine, the eyes of faith judge with right judgment and see the Lord himself.

quick: Paul: I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
He fears that clever preachers will bring another Jesus, another spirit, another gospel.
Jesus: my teaching is not mine but his who sent me; do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.
2027-06-26.action: Do one kind act this week for someone you have judged by appearance, and test every new preacher by the faith of the apostles.
2027-06-26.question: Whom have I judged by appearance this week?

family.explain: Some people in Jerusalem were surprised that Jesus could teach so well, because he had not studied in a famous school. They judged him by how he looked. Jesus said: my teaching comes from my Father. And he told them: do not judge by appearances. God looks at the heart. We should not decide that someone is good or bad because of their clothes, their colour, their house or the way they talk.
family.intention: We pray for children who are teased because of how they look, and for those who feel left out.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or in our street whom we have judged too quickly? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: A mother in Thrissur (a story told to illustrate the reading) was searching for a bride for her son, and she rejected one proposal after another by looking at the photographs: too dark, too short, family not well off. Her son was quiet about it. One evening her own mother, an old woman who had buried her husband young and raised five children on a teacher's salary, asked to see the photographs. She picked one that had been put aside and said, ‘Do you know this girl? She comes every Saturday to the palliative care unit at the parish and washes the old people's feet. I have seen her.’ Then she quoted the word of the Lord to Samuel: ‘The Lord looks on the heart.’ The mother went to meet the girl's family. A year later, at the wedding, it was the grandmother who placed the crown on the bride's head with the greatest joy.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, gather us as your bride. Keep our love for you sincere and pure, and open our eyes to see as you see. Amen.
share: I promised you in marriage to one husband (2 Corinthians 11:2). Is my love for Christ undivided?
Another Jesus… a different gospel (2 Corinthians 11:4). Which voices draw me away from the faith of the apostles?
My teaching is not mine but his who sent me (John 7:16). Do I seek God's glory or my own when I speak of him?
Do not judge by appearances (John 7:24). Whom have I judged unfairly?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us faithful to you.
interc: For the Church, bride of Christ, that she may remain pure in faith and generous in love.
For preachers, priests and catechists, that they may hand on the faith of the apostles and not their own opinions.
For those confused by false teachers and new sects, that they may find their way back to the fullness of the truth.
For all who suffer discrimination because of colour, caste, appearance or poverty.
For young people seeking a partner in marriage, that they and their families may look at the heart.
pm.close: Father, your Son did not seek his own glory but yours. Keep us faithful to his Gospel as the apostles handed it on, keep us from every rash judgment, and make your Church a pure bride for her Bridegroom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul writes to the Corinthians with the love of a father who has arranged his daughter's marriage: “I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Corinthians 11:2). The Church is the bride of Christ, and each of us belongs to that bride.

Paul is afraid. Clever preachers have come with fine words and a different Jesus: a Jesus without the Cross, a gospel of success. The Corinthians accepted them easily. We too hear many voices today, on our phones and in new groups. Let us test every voice by the faith of the apostles that the Church has kept.

In the Gospel, people are surprised: how can Jesus teach so well when he has not studied? Jesus says: “My teaching is not mine but his who sent me” (John 7:16). A true teacher does not seek his own glory but God's.
Then he says: “Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment” (John 7:24). We often judge by appearance: by colour, caste, dress, money, or a photograph. But God looks at the heart.

On this Saturday let us look to Mary, the humble Virgin of Nazareth, wholly devoted to Christ. May she keep our love for her Son sincere and pure, and give us eyes that see others as God sees them. Amen.
kids: Children, some people did not believe Jesus because he had not gone to a famous school. They looked only at the outside. Jesus said: do not judge by appearances! God looks at the heart. This week, be kind to someone others laugh at because of how they look.

intro: Theme: “Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.”
The Church as the bride promised to Christ, the danger of another Jesus and another gospel, and the right judgment that sees the heart.

points.h: Promised in marriage to one husband
sub: The Church, a bride and not a club.
q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly in prayer one evening this week.

sub: Staying with the faith of the apostles.
q: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you. They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the Lord.
But I am afraid that as the serpent deceived Eve by its cunning, your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ.
points.apply: Test one religious message you receive this week by the Creed and the teaching of the Church.

q: But the Lord said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.”
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment.
points.apply: Do one kind act for someone you had judged by appearance.

concl: We are a bride promised to Christ: let our devotion be sincere and pure, faithful to the Jesus of the apostles.
Like Mary, let us see as God sees, looking on the heart.
2027-06-26.resolve: This week, renew your love for Christ, test every new voice by the faith of the Church, and correct one rash judgment by an act of kindness.
